chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the mortgage (rahn), if it perishes in the possession of the mortgagee (murtahin) without his having destroyed it, the right returns to the mortgagor (rahin), so he takes it. But if he (the mortgagee) had destroyed it, the excess value is returned between the two of them.

key_terms.الرَّاهِن: The mortgagor or debtor who pledged the item
key_terms.الْمُرْتَهِن: The mortgagee or creditor holding the collateral
key_terms.يَسْتَهْلِكَهُ: He destroys it (implies fault or consumption)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mortgaged item that is lost or destroyed by the creditor?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the risk allocation in Islamic mortgage (rahn) by distinguishing between simple loss and destruction (istehlak) by the creditor. It establishes that while the debtor bears the risk of accidental loss, the creditor is liable for the surplus value if he consumes or destroys the item, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the holder of the collateral assumes responsibility for its preservation. This ruling ensures equity by preventing the creditor from unjustly enriching himself at the debtor's expense through the consumption of the pledged asset.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aban, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘With regards to the mortgage, when it perishes in the presence of the mortgagee from other than him having destroyed it, it would be returned in his right upon the mortgagor, so he would take it. So if he had destroyed it, the excess would be returned between the two of them’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-ffassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Aban from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “About al-Rahn (security deposit and mortgage), abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If loss takes place on the side of mortgagee without willingly consuming it, he asks the mortgager to provide compensation for his loss; but if he consumes it then both sides exchange the difference to each other.’”
